purpose: Hourly authoritative-vendor contingent-workforce integration delta. Adds Beeline Enterprise and Magnit VMS as distinct external-workforce systems with documented reusable REST-based integration paths, and records Beeline's newly launched MCP agent capability behind a separate action/security boundary. Evidence remains specification/public-documentation level only: no sandbox or customer tenant credentials were used and all writes remain disabled.

systems.name: Beeline Enterprise / VMS
systems.evidenceNote: Beeline documents a hybrid integration framework spanning RESTful APIs, webhooks, flat-file/data feeds, Reporting as a Service JSON APIs, plug-and-play connectors and iPaaS for cloud, SaaS and on-premises estates. Its public integration material states 300+ APIs and self-service developer/sandbox tooling, and documents API capacity up to 1,000 calls per minute per endpoint. The integration scope covers workforce lifecycle, hierarchy, cost centres, user roles, approvals, reporting, billing and invoicing. Beeline also launched a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) capability on 2 September 2026 for approved AI agents to discover and invoke governed workforce tools using Beeline identity/permissions; vendor examples include status lookup plus mutative approvals and candidate actions. MCP is therefore recorded as a potentially valuable agent/management capability but is deliberately not declared as a WFM connector protocol until its exact tool contract and read-only enforcement can be proved. These surfaces include mutative business workflows, so Manufacturing WFM must use narrowly scoped read credentials and keep candidate, assignment, approval, time, invoice, supplier and agent actions disabled until separately authorised and write-roundtrip certified. No Beeline sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.

systems.name: Magnit VMS / Magnit API
systems.evidenceNote: Magnit documents RESTful Client, Reporting as a Service (RaaS) and Gateway APIs. RaaS uses OAuth2-style bearer authentication backed by platform-managed Client Key, Client Secret and Credential Key values, has distinct US and EU endpoints, supports asynchronous request/status/retrieve report workflows, and paginates with lowercase page/size parameters (5,000 default, 20,000 maximum). Re-requesting the same report within 15 minutes returns the same Run ID, which can be used as an idempotency signal. API credentials default to 90-day validity with controlled overlap during rotation. Custom report column names become JSON keys, so per-client schema fingerprints are mandatory. Magnit's 2026 Gateway API Toolkit also supports direct system-to-system flow of job requests, candidate submissions, timesheets and billing data; those are write-capable supplier workflows and remain prohibited for the Manufacturing WFM read connector until separately authorised and certified. No Magnit sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.
